title: O-NET ม.6 ชุดฝึกที่ 1

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: At the school canteen

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Hi, Auntie Noi. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Auntie Noi
dialogue.text: Of course. With chicken or pork?

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Chicken, please, and not too spicy. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Auntie Noi
dialogue.text: Forty baht. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Oh no, I only have a 500-baht note. I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Auntie Noi
dialogue.text: Hmm, I don't have enough change yet. It's still early.

dialogue.speaker: Ken
dialogue.text: ___3___ I'll pay for it, and you can give me the money tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Thanks, Ken. You're a lifesaver!

options: Can I have a plate of fried rice, please?
I made some fried rice for you.
Have you ever cooked fried rice before?
Would you like a plate of fried rice today?
Where did you buy this fried rice?
items.explanationTh: แม่ค้าตอบว่า "Of course. With chicken or pork?" แสดงว่าพลอยกำลังขอสั่งอาหาร จึงต้องเป็นประโยคขอ "Can I have ..., please?" ส่วน "Would you like ...?" เป็นการเสนอให้ ซึ่งผิดบทบาทของผู้ซื้อ

options: Do you have the exact amount?
Would you like to order more?
items.explanationTh: พลอยตอบว่ามีแต่แบงก์ 500 บาท แสดงว่าแม่ค้าถามว่ามีเงินพอดีหรือไม่ (exact amount) ตัวเลือกอื่นไม่ทำให้พลอยต้องตอบเรื่องแบงก์ใหญ่
เคนพูดต่อว่า "I'll pay for it" แสดงว่าเขาเสนอความช่วยเหลือ จึงต้องเป็น "Don't worry. Let me help." ตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นการปฏิเสธหรือไม่เกี่ยวข้อง

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Asking the way

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Excuse me. ___4___

dialogue.speaker: Fah
dialogue.text: Sure. Go straight past the library and turn left at the basketball court.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Is it far from here?

dialogue.speaker: Fah
dialogue.text: ___5___ It's only about a three-minute walk.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Great. And is the meeting room on the ground floor?

dialogue.speaker: Fah
dialogue.text: No, it's on the second floor. ___6___

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: That's very kind of you. Thank you.

options: Why is the science building so far away from here?
Have you ever studied in the science building?
Do you know what time the science class starts?
Could you tell me where the science building is?
Would you like to visit the science building?
items.explanationTh: ฟ้าตอบด้วยการบอกทาง (Go straight ... turn left ...) ผู้มาเยือนจึงต้องถามทาง "Could you tell me where ... is?" ตัวเลือกอื่นไม่ได้ถามทาง
ประโยคถัดไปบอกว่าเดินแค่ 3 นาที จึงต้องตอบว่า "ไม่ค่อยไกล" (Not really) ส่วน "Yes, very far." และ "take a taxi" ขัดกับข้อมูลนี้

options: I'm not a student at this school.
The meeting finished an hour ago.
Please don't go upstairs without me.
items.explanationTh: ผู้มาเยือนตอบว่า "That's very kind of you" แสดงว่าฟ้าเสนอความช่วยเหลือ คือพาไปส่ง ตัวเลือกอื่นไม่ใช่ความมีน้ำใจที่ต้องขอบคุณ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Saying sorry

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: Jay, I'm really sorry. ___7___

dialogue.speaker: Jay
dialogue.text: Oh no! What happened to it?

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: My little brother dropped it on the floor, and now it won't turn on.

dialogue.speaker: Jay
dialogue.text: Well, ___8___ It was quite old anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: That's nice of you, but I'd still like to buy you a new one.

dialogue.speaker: Jay
dialogue.text: ___9___ We can go to the stationery shop together after school.

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: Sounds good. Thanks for being so understanding.

options: I can lend you my calculator.
items.explanationTh: แนทขอโทษ และเจย์ถามว่า "What happened to it?" ต่อมาบอกว่าเครื่องเปิดไม่ติด จึงต้องเป็นการสารภาพว่าทำเครื่องคิดเลขพัง

options: you must pay me back today.
items.explanationTh: เจย์พูดต่อว่า "It was quite old anyway" และแนทตอบว่า "That's nice of you" แสดงว่าเจย์ให้อภัย "these things happen" (เรื่องแบบนี้เกิดขึ้นได้)

options: Well, OK, if you really want to.
items.explanationTh: เจย์ชวนไปร้านเครื่องเขียนด้วยกันหลังเลิกเรียน แสดงว่ายอมรับข้อเสนอของแนทที่จะซื้อเครื่องใหม่ให้ "Well, OK, if you really want to." ส่วน "busy all week" ขัดกับการนัดไปด้วยกัน

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: An invitation

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: Pim, are you free this Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: I think so. ___10___

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: My cousin is opening a small bakery, and ___11___

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: I'd love to! What time should I be there?

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: The opening is at ten, but let's meet at the bus stop at half past nine.

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: ___12___ See you then.

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: Great. Don't forget to bring your camera!

items.explanationTh: ไหมตอบโดยอธิบายเหตุผลที่ถามว่าว่างไหม (ญาติเปิดร้านเบเกอรี่) จึงต้องถามว่า "Why do you ask?"

options: the cakes there are far too expensive.
would you like to come with me?
I have to stay home alone.
she doesn't know how to bake.
items.explanationTh: พิมตอบว่า "I'd love to!" ซึ่งเป็นการตอบรับคำชวน ดังนั้นช่องนี้ต้องเป็นคำชวน "would you like to come with me?"
พิมพูดต่อว่า "See you then." แสดงว่าตกลงตามเวลานัด "That works for me." (สะดวก/ได้เลย) ตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นการปฏิเสธหรือแสดงความเสียใจ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Choosing a project topic

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: We need to choose a topic for our class presentation. ___13___

dialogue.speaker: Tan
dialogue.text: How about street food in our town? Everybody loves it.

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: ___14___ But lots of groups chose food last year.

dialogue.speaker: Tan
dialogue.text: Good point. What about the old wooden shophouses on River Road?

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: That's a great idea! We could take photos and interview the owners.

dialogue.speaker: Tan
dialogue.text: ___15___ When should we start?

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: Let's go there on Sunday morning.

items.explanationTh: แทนตอบด้วยการเสนอหัวข้อ "How about street food ...?" จึงต้องเป็นคำถามขอความคิดเห็น "Do you have any ideas?"

options: It's nothing to do with me.
items.explanationTh: บีมเห็นด้วยบางส่วนก่อนแย้งด้วย "But ..." จึงใช้ "I see what you mean." (เข้าใจที่เธอพูด) ส่วน "You're absolutely wrong." ไม่เข้ากับคำว่า But ที่ตามมา

options: I'm not so sure about that.
items.explanationTh: แทนถามต่อทันทีว่า "When should we start?" แสดงว่าเห็นด้วยอย่างยิ่ง "I couldn't agree more." ตัวเลือกอื่นแสดงความไม่เห็นด้วย

groups.instructionTh: อ่านประกาศ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Green Leaf Weekend Market
groups.text:
GREEN LEAF WEEKEND MARKET
Every Saturday and Sunday, 7:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m.
Car park behind Ban Mai Sports Centre

Fresh vegetables from local farms, homemade snacks, second-hand books and handmade bags.

Please note:
• From 6 July, the market will close one hour later than usual.
• Bring your own bag. Sellers will charge 2 baht for each plastic bag.
• Dogs and other pets must be kept on a lead.
• Parking is free for the first two hours. After that, it costs 20 baht per hour.

Would you like to sell at the market? Call Khun Darin on 081-555-0192 before Thursday each week.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To invite farmers to a meeting
To teach people how to make handmade bags
To ask people to sell their pets
To give information about a market
To advertise a new sports centre
items.explanationTh: ประกาศบอกวัน เวลา สถานที่ สินค้า และกฎของตลาดนัดสุดสัปดาห์ จุดประสงค์จึงเป็นการให้ข้อมูลเกี่ยวกับตลาด

items.stem: What time will the market close from 6 July?
items.explanationTh: เดิมตลาดปิด 1:00 p.m. และประกาศบอกว่าตั้งแต่ 6 ก.ค. จะปิด "one hour later" จึงเป็น 2:00 p.m.

items.stem: If you park your car for three hours, how much will you pay?
items.explanationTh: จอดฟรีสองชั่วโมงแรก หลังจากนั้นชั่วโมงละ 20 บาท จอดสามชั่วโมงจึงจ่ายเฉพาะชั่วโมงที่สาม คือ 20 บาท

items.stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the notice?
options: The market is held inside the sports centre.
The market is open every day of the week.
Plastic bags are given out for free.
You can bring your dog if it is on a lead.
People who want to sell must call on Friday.
items.explanationTh: ประกาศเขียนว่า "Pets must be kept on a lead" จึงพาสุนัขมาได้ถ้าใส่สายจูง ส่วนถุงพลาสติกคิดใบละ 2 บาท ตลาดเปิดแค่เสาร์–อาทิตย์ และต้องโทรก่อนวันพฤหัสบดี

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: A message from the class teacher
groups.text:
Hi Grade 12/3,
This is a reminder about our trip to the Sri Wiang Paper Museum tomorrow. Because heavy rain is expected in the morning, the bus will leave at 8:30 instead of 8:00. Please meet in front of the school hall, not at the main gate. Wear your PE uniform and comfortable shoes, and bring a raincoat. Lunch will be provided by the museum, but you may bring your own snacks. Anyone who has not handed in the permission form must give it to me before 4 p.m. today. Without the form, you will not be able to join the trip.
See you tomorrow!
Ms. Kanya

items.stem: Why will the bus leave later than planned?
items.explanationTh: ข้อความบอกว่า "Because heavy rain is expected in the morning" รถจึงออกช้าลง สาเหตุคือสภาพอากาศ

items.stem: Where should the students meet tomorrow?
options: In front of the school hall
items.explanationTh: ครูเขียนว่า "meet in front of the school hall, not at the main gate" จึงต้องไปพบกันหน้าหอประชุม

items.stem: The word "provided" in the message is closest in meaning to ____.
items.explanationTh: "Lunch will be provided by the museum" หมายถึงพิพิธภัณฑ์จัดอาหารกลางวันให้ provided จึงใกล้เคียงกับ given (ให้/จัดให้)

items.stem: What will happen to a student who hands in the form at 5 p.m. today?
options: He or she will get a raincoat.
He or she must bring lunch.
He or she will sit at the front.
He or she cannot go on the trip.
He or she must pay extra.
items.explanationTh: ต้องส่งใบขออนุญาตก่อน 4 โมงเย็น และ "Without the form, you will not be able to join the trip" ส่งตอน 5 โมงจึงเลยกำหนดและไปทัศนศึกษาไม่ได้

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: An email from Thailand
groups.text:
Dear Grandma,

I can't believe I've already been in Thailand for a month! My host family, the Srisuks, are really kind. My host sister, Nam, is the same age as me, and for the first few weeks I sat on the back of her bicycle on the way to Ban Suan School. Last week, I finally learned to ride one myself, so now we cycle side by side. I fell off three times, but Nam never laughed at me.

School here starts early, at 7:30, and everyone stands in line for the flag ceremony first. At first I found the heat difficult, but now I'm getting used to it. My favourite subject is Thai. My teacher says my pronunciation is improving, but I still mix up the words for "near" and "far", which caused some funny problems when I gave directions to a visitor last Tuesday!

Last weekend I joined the school band. They needed someone who could play the trumpet, so I was lucky that I had packed mine before I left home. We are practising for a concert in December, and Nam's parents have already promised to come.

I miss your apple pie, but Thai mango sticky rice is a very good replacement. Please give my love to Grandpa.

Love,
Lena

items.stem: Which of the following has Lena NOT done yet?
options: Played in a concert with the band
items.explanationTh: เลนาเขียนว่า "We are practising for a concert in December" คอนเสิร์ตยังไม่เกิดขึ้น ส่วนการขี่จักรยาน เข้าวงดนตรี บอกทางเป็นภาษาไทย และกินข้าวเหนียวมะม่วง เธอทำไปแล้วทั้งหมด

items.stem: How does Lena get to school now?
options: She walks to school with Nam.
She takes the school bus with Nam.
She sits on the back of Nam's bicycle.
She rides a bicycle next to Nam.
items.explanationTh: ข้อความบอกว่าช่วงแรกนั่งซ้อนท้ายจักรยานของน้ำ แต่ "now we cycle side by side" ตอนนี้จึงปั่นจักรยานเองข้าง ๆ น้ำ

items.stem: The phrase "getting used to" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ____.
items.explanationTh: ตอนแรกเลนารู้สึกว่าอากาศร้อนลำบาก "but now I'm getting used to it" แปลว่าเริ่มคุ้นเคย คือ becoming comfortable with

items.stem: Why does Lena say she was lucky?
options: She had packed her own trumpet.
Her grandmother sent her a trumpet.
The band chose her as its leader.
She won a prize at a music concert.
Nam taught her to play the trumpet.
items.explanationTh: วงต้องการคนเป่าทรัมเป็ต และเลนาโชคดีที่ "I had packed mine before I left home" คือเอาทรัมเป็ตของตัวเองมาด้วย

items.stem: What does "which" in paragraph 2 refer to?
options: The visitor who came last Tuesday
items.explanationTh: "which caused some funny problems" ขยายสิ่งที่อยู่ก่อนหน้า คือการที่เลนาสับสนคำว่า "ใกล้" กับ "ไกล" จึงบอกทางผิดจนเกิดเรื่องตลก

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The Blue Umbrella
groups.text:
It was raining hard when Krit left his after-school maths class. He opened his blue umbrella and walked quickly to the bus stop. There, an old man was standing at the edge of the shelter, holding a large paper bag. The roof was small and the wind was blowing the rain in, so the bag was getting wetter and wetter.

"Excuse me, sir," Krit said. "Would you like to use my umbrella? My bus comes in two minutes, and my house is right next to the stop where I get off."

The man looked surprised. "But then you won't have one tomorrow."

"I'll borrow my sister's," Krit smiled. "Please take it."

The man thanked him many times and wrote Krit's name on the paper bag.

Two weeks later, the school had a special guest for Reading Week: a writer of children's books who had grown up in the town. When he walked onto the stage, Krit nearly dropped his pen. It was the old man from the bus stop! In his hand was a familiar blue umbrella.

"Before I begin," the writer said, "I need to return something to a very kind young man." The whole hall turned to look as Krit walked slowly to the stage, his face as red as a tomato.

items.stem: Why was the old man's bag getting wet?
options: There was a hole in the umbrella.
He had dropped it into a puddle.
The wind blew rain into the small shelter.
Krit splashed water on it by mistake.
He had been waiting for a taxi in the heavy rain.
items.explanationTh: เรื่องบอกว่า "The roof was small and the wind was blowing the rain in" ฝนจึงสาดเข้ามาในที่พักรอรถที่หลังคาเล็ก ทำให้ถุงเปียก

items.stem: Why did Krit think he would not need the umbrella?
options: He had another umbrella in his bag.
His older sister was coming to pick him up by car.
He thought the rain would stop soon.
He enjoyed walking in the rain.
He would not have to walk far after the bus.
items.explanationTh: กฤษบอกว่า "my house is right next to the stop where I get off" ลงรถแล้วบ้านอยู่ติดป้ายเลย จึงแทบไม่ต้องเดินตากฝน ส่วนร่มของพี่สาวเขาจะยืมในวันพรุ่งนี้

items.stem: Who was the old man?
items.explanationTh: แขกพิเศษในสัปดาห์การอ่านคือ "a writer of children's books" และกฤษจำได้ว่าเป็นชายชราที่ป้ายรถเมล์

items.stem: The phrase "his face as red as a tomato" shows that Krit felt ____.
items.explanationTh: ทั้งหอประชุมหันมามองขณะกฤษเดินขึ้นเวที หน้าแดงเหมือนมะเขือเทศจึงแสดงความเขินอาย (embarrassed) ไม่ใช่โกรธหรือป่วย

items.stem: Which sentence best describes the message of the story?
options: A small act of kindness can be remembered.
Old people should stay home when it rains.
Reading Week is the best school event.
Students should not lend their things.
items.explanationTh: กฤษให้ยืมร่มด้วยความมีน้ำใจ และนักเขียนจดชื่อไว้แล้วกลับมาขอบคุณต่อหน้าทุกคน แสดงว่าความใจดีเล็ก ๆ ถูกจดจำ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Saturdays at Little Lamp Books
groups.text:
Posted by Oat, 17

Three months ago, I started my first part-time job at Little Lamp Books, a small bookshop near my school. I work every Saturday from ten to four, and I earn 400 baht a day.

Before I started, I thought the job would be easy. I imagined myself sitting quietly and reading all day. I was wrong! In the morning I unpack boxes of new books and put price stickers on them. Then I help customers find what they are looking for, which is harder than it sounds. Last week, a woman asked for "the green book about a cat". She didn't know the title or the writer. After twenty minutes of searching, we finally found it. She was so happy that she bought two more books.

The owner, Khun Rattana, has taught me a lot. She says a good shop assistant listens first and talks second. I have also become better at maths, because I count the money at the end of each day.

The best part of the job? Every month I can choose one book to take home for free. So far I have chosen a travel guide to Laos, a comic about space and a cookbook for my mum.

If you are thinking about getting a weekend job, my advice is simple: don't expect it to be easy, but expect to learn a lot.

items.stem: How many hours does Oat work each Saturday?
items.explanationTh: โอ๊ตทำงาน "from ten to four" คือ 10 โมงถึง 4 โมงเย็น รวม 6 ชั่วโมง

items.stem: What did Oat believe before he started the job?
options: He would have no time to read.
He would have to count money.
It would not be hard work.
items.explanationTh: เขาเขียนว่า "I thought the job would be easy" และคิดว่าจะได้นั่งอ่านหนังสือทั้งวัน จึงเชื่อว่างานไม่หนัก

items.stem: Why did the woman most likely buy two more books?
options: Oat asked her to buy more.
She wanted gifts for her cat.
The books were on sale that week.
She had lost the green book.
She was pleased with Oat's help.
items.explanationTh: หลังจากโอ๊ตช่วยหาหนังสือนาน 20 นาทีจนเจอ "She was so happy that she bought two more books" แสดงว่าพอใจกับความช่วยเหลือ

items.stem: What does Khun Rattana mean by "listens first and talks second"?
options: Never say anything to the customers
Read every book before helping any customer
Speak only when the shop owner is nearby
Talk more than customers so they feel welcome
Find out what customers need before speaking

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Board Game Cafés
groups.text:
In many cities, a new kind of café is becoming popular with teenagers and families: the board game café. Customers pay a small fee, usually 60 to 100 baht per person, and can then play any game from a large collection for as long as they like. Drinks and snacks are sold separately.

"People come here to talk face to face," says Jaruwan Mekha, who opened Two Moons Café in Phitsanulok two years ago. "At most tables, nobody looks at their phone for hours." Her café has over 400 games, from simple card games for young children to long strategy games that can take a whole afternoon.

Choosing a game can be difficult for new customers, so many cafés employ "game guides". These staff members recommend a suitable game for each group and explain the rules, so players do not have to read a thick instruction book.

Teachers have also noticed the benefits. Some games require players to plan ahead, solve problems and work as a team, and a few schools now hold board game clubs after class. However, not everyone is a fan. Some parents say the cafés are too noisy for studying, and some customers complain that the best games are always taken at weekends.

Still, the success of these cafés shows that, even in a digital world, people enjoy simply sitting around a table together.

items.stem: Which statement about Two Moons Café is TRUE?
options: It does not allow phones at tables.
It has games for young children too.
Its fee includes drinks and snacks.
items.explanationTh: ร้านมีเกม "from simple card games for young children to long strategy games" จึงมีเกมสำหรับเด็กเล็กด้วย ส่วนร้านเปิดมาสองปี มีเกมมากกว่า 400 เกม เครื่องดื่มขายแยก และไม่ได้ห้ามใช้โทรศัพท์

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Songkran: Having Fun Politely
groups.text:
Songkran, the Thai New Year, takes place from 13 to 15 April, during the hottest time of the year. For many visitors, it is famous as a huge water festival. But Songkran is not only about water fights. It is also a time for families to get together and to show respect to older people.

In many homes, younger family members gently pour scented water over the hands of their parents and grandparents. This custom is called rod nam dam hua. In return, the elders give them good wishes for the new year. Many people also clean their houses at this time as a way of starting the year fresh.

If you plan to join the water fun in the streets, there are a few simple rules to remember. First, only splash people who are clearly playing. Elderly people, people carrying babies and anyone in a work uniform, such as a delivery rider, should be left dry. Second, use clean water and never throw ice, which can hurt. Third, do not aim at the face of a person on a motorbike, because it can cause an accident. Finally, put your phone in a waterproof bag. Keeping it dry is your own responsibility, not other people's!

Many towns now have "Songkran zones" where water play is allowed, and quiet areas where it is not. Some organisers also ask players to save water by using small buckets instead of hoses.

If someone splashes you and you do not want to play, simply smile and say "Sawasdee pee mai!" – Happy New Year. A friendly smile is the best way to enjoy Songkran, wet or dry.

items.stem: What is paragraph 3 mainly about?
options: Places where water play is not allowed
Ways that families show respect to elders
Rules to follow when playing with water
How to greet people who want to stay dry
Reasons why Songkran takes place in April
items.explanationTh: ย่อหน้าที่ 3 ขึ้นต้นว่า "there are a few simple rules to remember" แล้วบอกกฎ First–Finally ในการเล่นน้ำ ส่วนการเคารพผู้ใหญ่อยู่ย่อหน้า 2 และโซนเงียบอยู่ย่อหน้า 4

items.explanationTh: ในพิธีรดน้ำดำหัว ลูกหลานรดน้ำที่มือผู้ใหญ่ และ "the elders give them good wishes" คือผู้ใหญ่ให้พร

items.stem: According to the passage, who should NOT be splashed?
options: A teenager in a Songkran zone

items.explanationTh: บทความระบุว่า "anyone in a work uniform, such as a delivery rider, should be left dry" ส่วนตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นคนที่กำลังเล่นน้ำอยู่

items.explanationTh: การเก็บโทรศัพท์ไม่ให้เปียกเป็น "your own responsibility, not other people's" คือหน้าที่ของเราเอง จึงตรงกับ duty

items.stem: Why do some organisers ask players to use small buckets?
options: To make the water fights longer

items.explanationTh: ผู้จัดขอให้ใช้ขันหรือถังเล็กแทนสายยาง "to save water" คือเพื่อประหยัดน้ำ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: How Plants Make Their Own Food
groups.text:
Humans and animals need to eat to get energy, but green plants are different. They can make their own food through a process called photosynthesis. The word comes from two Greek parts: "photo", meaning light, and "synthesis", meaning putting together.

Photosynthesis takes place mainly in the leaves. Inside leaf cells there are tiny parts called chloroplasts. They contain a green substance called chlorophyll, which gives plants their colour and captures energy from sunlight.

To make food, a plant needs three things. It takes in water from the soil through its roots. It takes in carbon dioxide, a gas in the air, through very small holes in its leaves. And it uses the energy of sunlight, which is captured by chlorophyll. With these, the plant produces glucose, a type of sugar. Some of the glucose is used right away for energy, and some is stored, for example as starch in potatoes and rice grains.

Photosynthesis also gives off oxygen as a by-product. This oxygen goes out through the leaves into the air, and it is the same oxygen that humans and animals breathe.

Because plants need light, photosynthesis stops at night. This is why a houseplant kept in a dark corner may slowly turn yellow and weak. Scientists say that almost all life on Earth depends, directly or indirectly, on photosynthesis: plants feed animals, and those animals feed other animals.

items.stem: According to the passage, what does "synthesis" mean?
items.explanationTh: บทความอธิบายว่า "'synthesis', meaning putting together" ส่วน light เป็นความหมายของ photo

items.stem: What is the job of chlorophyll?
options: To make small holes in leaves
To turn leaves yellow at night
To carry water from the roots
To store sugar in rice grains
items.explanationTh: คลอโรฟิลล์ "gives plants their colour and captures energy from sunlight" คือดักจับพลังงานจากแสงอาทิตย์

items.stem: How does carbon dioxide get into a plant?
options: Through tiny holes in the leaves
From the light of the sun
From the starch in its roots
items.explanationTh: พืชรับคาร์บอนไดออกไซด์ "through very small holes in its leaves" ส่วนรากใช้ดูดน้ำ

items.stem: What happens to the glucose that a plant makes?
options: All of it is kept in the roots for night.
It is changed back into carbon dioxide.
Some is used at once and some is stored.
All of it is given off through the leaves.
It is sent down into the soil for later.
items.explanationTh: บทความบอกว่า "Some of the glucose is used right away for energy, and some is stored" เช่น เก็บเป็นแป้งในมันฝรั่งและเมล็ดข้าว ส่วนสิ่งที่ปล่อยออกทางใบคือออกซิเจน

options: a thing that is bought nearby

items.explanationTh: ผลผลิตหลักคือกลูโคส ส่วนออกซิเจนเป็น "by-product" คือผลพลอยได้ที่เกิดขึ้นเพิ่มเติม และเป็นประโยชน์ต่อคนและสัตว์ จึงไม่ใช่สิ่งที่เป็นอันตราย

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: From Shells to Smartphones: A Short History of Money
groups.text:
Long ago, people did not use money. If a farmer had rice but wanted fish, he had to find a fisherman who wanted rice. This system is called barter. It worked in small villages, but it had a big problem: both people had to want what the other person had at the same time.

To solve this, people began to use objects that everyone agreed were valuable. In different parts of the world, these included shells, salt, cloth and beads. Cowrie shells, for example, were used in parts of Asia and Africa for hundreds of years because they were small, strong and hard to copy.

Later, metal coins appeared. Coins were easy to carry and count, and they did not break or go bad like salt or cloth. Paper money came next. It was much lighter than a bag of coins, which made trade between distant cities easier.

Today, many people rarely touch cash at all. They pay with bank cards or by scanning a code with their smartphones. However, the basic idea of money has not changed. Whether it is a shell or a number on a screen, money only works because people trust that others will accept it.

Some experts think cash may disappear one day. Others point out that many older people and people in the countryside still depend on it, so coins and notes will probably stay with us for some time.

items.stem: What was the main problem with barter?
options: Farmers always had too much rice.
Fish always went bad before it could be traded.
It was only used in large cities.
Both sides had to want each other's goods.
items.explanationTh: ปัญหาของการแลกเปลี่ยนสินค้าคือ "both people had to want what the other person had at the same time" ทั้งสองฝ่ายต้องต้องการของของอีกฝ่ายพร้อมกัน

items.stem: Why were cowrie shells used as money?
options: They could be eaten when needed.
Only kings were able to collect them.
They were lighter than paper notes.
They were strong and difficult to copy.
items.explanationTh: เปลือกหอยเบี้ยถูกใช้เพราะ "small, strong and hard to copy" คือแข็งแรงและปลอมยาก ไม่ใช่เพราะใหญ่

items.stem: According to the passage, coins were better than salt because they ____.
items.explanationTh: เหรียญ "did not break or go bad like salt or cloth" คือไม่เสื่อมเสียเหมือนเกลือ ส่วนธนบัตรต่างหากที่เบากว่าเหรียญ

items.explanationTh: ประโยค "money only works because people trust that others will accept it" คำว่า it หมายถึง money คือคนเชื่อว่าคนอื่นจะยอมรับเงินนั้น

options: Older people have started to prefer cards.

items.explanationTh: ย่อหน้าสุดท้ายบอกว่ามีผู้เชี่ยวชาญบางคน (ไม่ใช่ส่วนใหญ่) คิดว่าเงินสดอาจหายไป แต่คนสูงอายุและคนในชนบทยังพึ่งพาเงินสด "so coins and notes will probably stay with us for some time" จึงสรุปได้ว่าเงินสดคงไม่หายไปเร็ว ๆ นี้

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Ban Nong Bua Says No to Plastic
groups.text:
Two years ago, the small community of Ban Nong Bua had a problem that everyone could see. Plastic bags hung in the trees, bottles floated in the canal, and the monthly community fair left piles of foam boxes behind it.

The change began with a group of Grade 11 students from Nong Bua Witthaya School. For a science project, they collected all the rubbish along 500 metres of the canal in one morning. They counted more than 1,200 pieces of plastic. When they shared their photos at a village meeting, many adults were shocked.

The students and the village committee then started the "Bring It Back" project. Every household received two cloth bags made by a local sewing group. Food sellers agreed to stop giving out foam boxes and to offer a 2-baht discount to customers who brought their own containers. A refill station was set up at the community centre, where people can buy dish soap and cooking oil by weight in their own bottles.

Not everything went smoothly. In the first few months, some sellers lost customers who were in a hurry and had forgotten their containers. To solve this, the project placed boxes of clean containers at the market, which people can borrow and return the next time.

Today, according to the committee's own count, plastic waste in the canal has fallen by about 70 percent, and nearby villages have started sending visitors to learn from Ban Nong Bua. "We are not perfect," says Somjai Rakdee, the committee leader. "But we have shown that small changes, made by everyone together, can make a big difference."

items.stem: Who started the change in Ban Nong Bua?
options: The food sellers at the fair

items.explanationTh: บทความบอกว่า "The change began with a group of Grade 11 students" คือนักเรียนชั้น ม.5 เป็นผู้เริ่มต้น
